title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: THE WRONG PIE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Nora Pickett, a DMV clerk from Bakersfield, California.
For twenty years, Nora was the head pie judge at the county fair.
And this year, she gave the blue ribbon to the wrong pie.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE MIX-UP
segments.quote: If you tell the truth, you don't have to remember anything.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: The winner was pie number forty-one. Nora wrote down fourteen.
Her reading glasses were on top of her head. I know the feeling.
By Sunday, the whole town knew. So Nora made up excuses. The tags fell off. The sun was in her eyes.
Her husband Ray just quoted Mark Twain:
If you tell the truth, you don't have to remember anything.
Nora tore up her excuses.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE MICROPHONE
segments.quote: How few there are who have courage enough to own their faults, or resolution enough to mend them.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: Telling Ray was easy. Telling the whole county was not.
At work, a Ben Franklin calendar hung by the photo booth. It said:
How few there are who have courage enough to own their faults, or resolution enough to mend them.
So at the fair, Nora took the microphone. I got it wrong, she said. I'm sorry. I'll fix it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE PEACH PIE
segments.quote: Persuasion is often more effectual than force.
segments.author: Aesop
lines: The real winner was Inez Duarte and her famous peach pie.
Inez would not open her door. Nora knocked, and knocked, and talked louder.
Then she remembered Aesop's fable, where the gentle sun beats the angry wind:
Persuasion is often more effectual than force.
So Nora stopped knocking. She left the blue ribbon on the porch, with a note. Yours. It always was.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE NEW RULES
segments.quote: It is common sense to take a method and try it. If it fails, admit it frankly and try another.
segments.author: Franklin D. Roosevelt
lines: Next, Nora fixed the judging. First idea: names on the pie tins in marker.
At the practice bake-off, the marker melted. Every pie was named Smudge.
Ray read her a line from President Franklin Roosevelt:
It is common sense to take a method and try it. If it fails, admit it frankly and try another.
So she did. Numbered plates. Two judges. Reading glasses on a chain.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE DRAWER
segments.quote: We learn wisdom from failure much more than from success.
segments.author: Samuel Smiles
lines: Back at the DMV, a young clerk named Kyle mixed up two forms, and hid them in a drawer.
Nora told him a line from Samuel Smiles, an old Scottish writer:
We learn wisdom from failure much more than from success.
Kyle fixed the forms. Nora bought him pie.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE NEXT FAIR
segments.quote: A life spent in making mistakes is not only more honorable, but more useful than a life spent doing nothing.
segments.author: George Bernard Shaw
lines: Then the fair board offered Nora a safe way out. Retire. No more mistakes.
She almost said yes. Then Inez sent a card, quoting the playwright George Bernard Shaw:
A life spent in making mistakes is not only more honorable, but more useful than a life spent doing nothing.
So Nora stayed. And now she has a co-judge. Inez Duarte.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Tell the truth. Own it. Be gentle. Try again. Learn. Keep going.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Tell the truth. Own it. Be gentle. Try another way. Learn. And keep showing up.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And check where your glasses are.
